items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to excluding certain amateur radio station operators from provisions of law relating to the use of portable electronic devices while operating a motor vehicle
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5674

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in
relation to excluding certain amateur radio station operators from
provisions of law relating to the use of portable electronic devices
while operating a motor vehicle

PURPOSE OF BILL: To exclude amateur radio license holders from
restrictions prohibiting the use of a portable electronic device while
such vehicle is in motion during a governmentally declared emergency.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS: Section 1 amends subdivision three of
section 1225-d, excluding a driver who holds an unrevoked and
unexpired official amateur radio station license or operator's license
issued by the Federal Communications Commission of the United States,
using two-way or citizens band radio services or two-way mobile radio
transmitter or receivers for licensees of the Federal Communications
Commission in the amateur radio service during a governmentally
declared emergency from restrictions prohibiting the use of portable
mobile devices while operating a motor vehicle.

Section two sets the enacting date.

JUSTIFICATION: During the event of an emergency, certain forms of
communications may be inoperable. In these instances, amateur radio
services are crucial as they allow for flow of vital information to
protect our citizens. This bill will exempt a driver who holds a
amateur radio station license or operator's license from the use of a
radio transmitter or receiver during a governmentally declared
emergency.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None to the state.

EFFECTIVE DATE: This act shall take immediately.

summary: Excludes certain amateur radio station operators from provisions of law relating to the use of portable electronic devices while operating a motor vehicle.
